church-of-east.self: Sees itself as the church Christ founded through the apostles Thomas, Addai, and Mari, continuing without a break in the faith of Nicea.

oriental-orthodox.self: Sees itself as the church Christ founded through the apostles, continuing without a break in the faith of the first three councils and Cyril.

eastern-orthodox.self: Sees itself as the church Christ founded through the apostles, continuing without a break through apostolic succession and the faith of the seven councils.
sources: Damick ch1: HOW THE ORTHODOX CHURCH VIEWS THE NON-ORTHODOX

catholic.self: Sees itself as the church Christ founded through the apostles, continuing without a break through bishops in communion with the pope, Peter's successor.

lutheran.self: Sees itself as the catholic church reformed by the gospel, keeping the ancient creeds and teaching nothing contrary to Scripture or the church catholic.

reformed.self: Sees itself as the catholic church reformed according to the word of God, holding the faith of the ancient church without later additions.

anabaptist.self: Sees itself as recovering the church of the New Testament, a community of disciples following Jesus and baptized on confession of faith.

anglican.self: Sees itself as part of the one catholic and apostolic church, reformed in the 1500s, keeping the ancient creeds and bishops in historic succession.

methodist.self: Sees itself as a renewal movement born within the Church of England, continuing the apostolic faith as part of the universal church.
sources: Damick ch3: Anglicanism and its Heirs

pentecostal.self: Sees itself as restoring the apostolic faith of Acts, with the Spirit's gifts, such as tongues and healing, renewed in the church.
sources: Damick ch6: The Apostolic Faith Movement

baptist.self: Holds that a New Testament church is a local congregation of believers baptized after professing faith in Christ.

evangelical-nondenom.self: Holds that Christ's church unites believers in him, with independent congregations guided by the Bible as God's authoritative word.
